terms.comment: The state of the miser, often in the plural for one’s troubles.
Toil and trouble that weighs one down; an old word, frequent in comedy.

phrases.latin: nam invidēre aliī bene esse, tibi male esse, miseriast
phrases.english: for to envy another his good fortune while you fare badly is misery

sources: Lewis & Short: miseria · Lewis & Short: aerumna
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
